title: Consequences of the axioms

proof.text: *Clause (1): $F$ is faithful.* Let $a,b:X\to Y$ with $F(a)=F(b)$. By axiom (1) of [def-galois-category] ([def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]) the equalizer $e:E\to X$ of $a,b$ exists. By axiom (4) $F$ is exact ([def-galois-exact-functor]), so $F(e):F(E)\to F(X)$ is an equalizer of $F(a),F(b)$ in $\mathbf{Sets}$, i.e. a bijection of $F(E)$ onto $\{t\in F(X):F(a)(t)=F(b)(t)\}=F(X)$. As $F$ reflects isomorphisms ([def-galois-reflects-isomorphisms]), $e$ is an isomorphism; then $a\circ e=b\circ e$ gives $a=b$ after composing with $e^{-1}$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), proof of (1)

proof.text: *Clause (2): monomorphisms and epimorphisms.* By axiom (1) of [def-galois-category], $\mathcal C$ has fibre products and pushouts (finite limits and colimits, [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]); by axiom (4), $F$ commutes with them ($F$ exact, [def-galois-exact-functor]) and reflects isomorphisms ([def-galois-reflects-isomorphisms]). So [lem-galois-mono-iff-injective] applies to $F$ and gives: $f:X\to Y$ is a monomorphism iff $F(f)$ is injective (Stacks' argument: $F$ carries the diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ to $F(X)\to F(X)\times_{F(Y)}F(X)$); and [lem-galois-epi-iff-surjective] applies and gives: $f$ is an epimorphism iff $F(f)$ is surjective (Stacks: $F$ carries $Y\amalg_XY\to Y$ to $F(Y)\amalg_{F(X)}F(Y)\to F(Y)$).

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), proofs of (2) and (3)

proof.text: *Clause (3): initial and final objects.* By axiom (1) of [def-galois-category] the empty diagram has a colimit $A$ and a limit $Z$ in $\mathcal C$ ([def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]); $A$ is initial and $Z$ is final ([def-galois-initial-mono], [def-galois-epi-final]). $F$ is exact ([def-galois-exact-functor]), so $F(A)$ is a colimit of the empty diagram in $\mathbf{Sets}$, i.e. $F(A)=\emptyset$, and $F(Z)$ is a limit of the empty diagram, i.e. a singleton. An initial (final) object $X$ is isomorphic to $A$ (to $Z$), so $F(X)$ is empty (a singleton). Conversely, if $F(X)=\emptyset$, the unique morphism $A\to X$ is carried to the bijection $\emptyset\to\emptyset$, so it is an isomorphism because $F$ reflects isomorphisms ([def-galois-reflects-isomorphisms]), and $X\cong A$ is initial. If $F(X)$ is a singleton, the unique morphism $X\to Z$ is carried to a map between singletons, a bijection, so $X\to Z$ is an isomorphism and $X$ is final. In particular (used below): an object $W$ with $F(W)\neq\emptyset$ is not initial, and a connected object $X$ ([def-galois-connected-object]), being not initial, has $F(X)\neq\emptyset$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), proofs of (4) and (5)

proof.text: *Clause (4): a morphism $f:X\to Y$ between connected objects is an epimorphism.* Let $i_1,i_2:Y\to Y\amalg_XY$ be the coprojections of the pushout of $f$ along $f$ and $e:E\to Y$ the equalizer of $i_1,i_2$ (both exist by axiom (1) of [def-galois-category], [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]). An equalizer morphism is a monomorphism ([def-galois-initial-mono]): two morphisms $u,v:W\to E$ with $e\circ u=e\circ v$ are both the unique factorization of $e\circ u$ through $e$. Since $i_1\circ f=i_2\circ f$, $f$ factors as $f=e\circ g$ with $g:X\to E$. $X$ is connected, so $F(X)\neq\emptyset$ (step 3), hence $F(E)\supseteq F(g)(F(X))$ is nonempty and $E$ is not initial (step 3). As $Y$ is connected ([def-galois-connected-object]) and $e$ is a monomorphism with non-initial source, $e$ is an isomorphism. From $i_1\circ e=i_2\circ e$ we get $i_1=i_2$, and [lem-galois-epi-iff-cokernel-pair] gives that $f$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), proof of (6)

proof.text: *Clause (5): if $X$ is connected and $a,b:X\to Y$ satisfy $F(a)(s)=F(b)(s)$ for one $s\in F(X)$, then $a=b$.* Let $e:E\to X$ be the equalizer of $a,b$ (axiom (1) of [def-galois-category], [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]); it is a monomorphism (as in step 4). $F$ is exact ([def-galois-exact-functor]), so $F(e)$ maps $F(E)$ bijectively onto $\{t\in F(X):F(a)(t)=F(b)(t)\}$, which contains $s$. Hence $F(E)\neq\emptyset$ and $E$ is not initial (step 3). As $X$ is connected ([def-galois-connected-object]), $e$ is an isomorphism, and $a\circ e=b\circ e$ gives $a=b$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), proof of (7) (label item-one-element)

proof.text: *Clause (6): automorphisms of a connected object.* Let $X$ be connected and $s\in F(X)$ (such $s$ exist, step 3). If $g,h\in\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ satisfy $F(g)(s)=F(h)(s)$, then $g=h$ by step 5 applied to $g,h:X\to X$; so $g\mapsto F(g)(s)$ is injective and $\#\operatorname{Aut}(X)\le\#F(X)$, a finite number by axiom (3) of [def-galois-category]. Since $F(X)$ is finite, the injective map $g\mapsto F(g)(s)$ is bijective iff $\#\operatorname{Aut}(X)=\#F(X)$; it is surjective iff the orbit of $s$ under $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ (acting through $g\mapsto F(g)$) is all of $F(X)$, i.e. iff $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ acts transitively on $F(X)$. So equality holds iff the action is transitive, which is the stated equivalence in the definition of a Galois object.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), paragraph after the proof ('By the lemma above we see that ... the automorphism group Aut(X) has order at most |F(X)| ... We say X is Galois if equality holds. Equivalently, X is Galois if it is connected and Aut(X) acts transitively on F(X)')

proof.text: *Clause (7): morphisms between coproducts of connected objects* are given by a map of index sets and morphisms of the components: this is [lem-galois-coproduct-morphism-components].

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN0 (label lemma-epi-mono), item (8) and proof of (8)

lean.statement: theorem stacksGaloisCategory_axioms {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w) (hG : IsStacksGaloisCategory F) : Functor.Faithful F ∧ (∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), (Mono f ↔ Function.Injective (F.map f)) ∧ (Epi f ↔ Function.Surjective (F.map f))) ∧ (∀ X : C, (Nonempty (IsInitial X) ↔ IsEmpty (F.obj X)) ∧ (Nonempty (IsTerminal X) ↔ ∃ s : F.obj X, ∀ t : F.obj X, t = s)) ∧ (∀ {X Y : C}, IsConnected X → IsConnected Y → ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, Epi f) ∧ (∀ {X Y : C}, IsConnected X → ∀ (a b : X ⟶ Y) (s : F.obj X), F.map a s = F.map b s → a = b) ∧ (∀ X : C, IsConnected X → ∀ s : F.obj X, Function.Injective (fun g : Aut X => F.map g.hom s) ∧ Nat.card (Aut X) ≤ Nat.card (F.obj X) ∧ (IsStacksGaloisObject F X ↔ Nat.card (Aut X) = Nat.card (F.obj X)) ∧ (IsStacksGaloisObject F X ↔ ∀ t : F.obj X, ∃ g : Aut X, F.map g.hom s = t)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type wI) (J : Type wJ) [Finite I] [Finite J] (Xi : I → C) (Yj : J → C) (X Y : C) (ιX : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X) (ιY : ∀ j, Yj j ⟶ Y), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk X ιX)) → Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y ιY)) → (∀ i, IsConnected (Xi i)) → (∀ j, IsConnected (Yj j)) → ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, ∃ (α : I → J) (component : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ Yj (α i)), ∀ i, ιX i ≫ f = component i ≫ ιY (α i))
